title: Find the number with no partner
hook: All but one number in 7 3 5 4 5 3 4 has a twin. Find it without sorting or counting.

doesNotKnow: that a XOR a is 0 and a XOR 0 is a
that XOR ignores order, so one pass finds the lone value

misconception: Finding the one number without a partner in a list needs sorting or a table of counts.
objective: The learner can fold 7 3 5 4 5 3 4 with XOR one number at a time, see pairs switch their bits back off and the running value end at 7 in any order, and explain why (a XOR a = 0, a XOR 0 = a, order does not matter).

claims.text: XOR of 7 3 5 4 5 3 4 is 7, written 111 in binary.
claims.source: Builder's node check (2026-10-14): [7,3,5,4,5,3,4].reduce(^) = 7; also 7 on 1,000 seeded random shuffles. Demo.tsx RESULT recomputes it. Unverified.

claims.text: a XOR a = 0 and a XOR 0 = a, so when a number's partner arrives, the bits it switched on switch back off.
claims.source: Bitwise: each bit of a XOR a is b XOR b = 0; each bit of a XOR 0 is b. Unverified.

claims.text: XOR ignores order, so any order of the list ends at 7.
claims.source: XOR is associative and commutative (bitwise addition mod 2). The stage's 'New order' button reshuffles with mulberry32 seeds 1001, 1002, ... (seeds not chosen to show anything; every order gives 7). Unverified.
Builder's node check (2026-10-14): 4^1^2^1^2 = 4. Demo.tsx OTHER_RESULT recomputes it. Unverified.

claims.text: It needs every other number to appear an even number of times; one that appears three times does not cancel and spoils the answer.
claims.source: The XOR of a list is the XOR of the values that appear an odd number of times (pairs cancel by c2). A value appearing 3 times leaves one copy, so the result is lone XOR that value. Node example: 5 5 5 7 7 gives 5, and 5 5 5 7 2 2 gives 2, not 7. Unverified.

claims.text: Finding the lone number this way takes one pass, with no sorting and no table of counts.
claims.source: One XOR per element, one running value of storage. Unverified.

recall.question: A list holds 1,001 numbers. Every number appears exactly twice except one. You XOR all of them together. What is left?
options: It depends on the order of the list
recall.why: Each pair XORs to 0 (a XOR a = 0), XOR ignores order, and the lone number XOR 0 is itself.
